pool.question: Who qualifies for Medicare, the federal health insurance program?
choices: ALL people 65 and older, plus people under 65 with certain disabilities
Only people who work for the government
Only people with limited income
Only veterans and their families
pool.explanation: ALL people 65 and older qualify for Medicare, plus people under 65 with certain disabilities.

pool.question: Who runs Medicaid?
choices: The VA
Only the federal government
Each individual state, with state and federal funding
Private insurance companies
pool.explanation: Medicaid is state and federally funded and run by each state.

pool.question: Medicaid coverage is mainly based on what?
choices: Military service
Limited income
Age 65 or older
Employer coverage
pool.explanation: Medicaid provides coverage for people with limited income.

pool.question: What does Medicare Part A mainly help cover?
choices: Prescription drugs
Hospital care, like inpatient stays
Dental cleanings only
Groceries
pool.explanation: Part A is Hospital Insurance.

pool.question: What does Medicare Part B mainly help cover?
choices: Prescription drugs only
Utilities
Medical care, like doctor visits and outpatient care
Inpatient hospital stays only
pool.explanation: Part B is Medical Insurance.

pool.question: What does the red, white and blue card prove?
choices: The consumer has Medicare and shows Part A, Part B, or both
The consumer has Medicaid
The consumer has a food card
The consumer is a veteran
pool.explanation: It is the Medicare card.

pool.question: Why does the script ask whether the consumer receives Medicaid?
choices: People with both Medicare and Medicaid may have different plan options
To check their income level exactly
Medicaid is a DQ
To mail them Medicaid forms
pool.explanation: It is information for the specialist. Yes or no continues.

pool.question: What might the healthy food card help with?
choices: Hospital bills only
Car repairs
Groceries on a monthly basis
Rent payments
pool.explanation: The healthy food card is there to help with groceries monthly, in plans that include it.

pool.question: What expenses might a Flex Card help cover?
choices: Dental, hearing, vision and utilities
Only prescriptions
Mortgage payments
Only groceries
pool.explanation: The Flex Card covers expenses such as dental, hearing, vision and utilities, in plans that include it.

pool.question: What is the Part B giveback?
choices: A bonus for fronters
A yearly check every Medicare member gets
A benefit some plans may have that helps cover some or all of the Part B premium
A Medicaid refund
pool.explanation: Some plans may include it. Never guaranteed.

pool.question: Are extra benefits like the food card guaranteed?
choices: No, they vary by plan, area and eligibility
Yes, if they have Medicaid
Yes, once they are transferred
Yes, for everyone with Parts A and B
pool.explanation: Nothing is guaranteed. That's why you say may.

pool.question: A consumer asks the dollar amount of a benefit. What is correct?
choices: Give the most common amount
You never give dollar amounts; that's a question for the agent
Give the highest possible amount to keep them interested
Say it's the same for everyone
pool.explanation: Never state dollar amounts.

pool.question: What does the licensed specialist do?
choices: Changes the plan without asking
Works for the government
Collects banking information
Reviews coverage and compares plan options that may be available
pool.explanation: The specialist reviews and compares. Only the consumer decides.

pool.question: Who can decide to change the consumer's insurance?
choices: Only the consumer
The fronter
Medicare
The specialist, automatically
pool.explanation: Changing insurance is ONLY something the consumer can do.

pool.question: Which consumer must be disqualified?
choices: Says they're busy
Has insurance through their employer
Has Medicaid and Medicare
Doesn't know what Parts A and B mean but has the card
pool.explanation: Work insurance is a DQ.

pool.question: Which consumer must be disqualified?
choices: Lives in a different state than expected
Asks who you are with
Has CHAMPVA
Lost their red, white and blue card
pool.explanation: CHAMPVA is military coverage, a DQ.

pool.question: Which consumer must be disqualified?
choices: Receives Medicaid
Covered by a Native American tribe
Is on a fixed income
Asks how you got their information
pool.explanation: Tribal coverage is a DQ.

pool.question: Which consumer must be disqualified?
choices: Has Tricare for Life
Says "I already have it"
Has Medicare Parts A and B only
Says "I'm not interested"
pool.explanation: Tricare for Life is a DQ.

pool.question: Which consumer must be disqualified?
choices: Is suspicious of scams
Doesn't have Medicare Parts A and B
Has Medicaid
Wants to know the benefits
pool.explanation: No Parts A and B is a DQ.

pool.question: Why are consumers with employer, retiree or military coverage disqualified?
choices: They are always too young
They are always on Medicaid
Their coverage works with Medicare in its own way and changing plans could affect it; this review isn't built for them
They already have a food card
pool.explanation: These coverages are not a fit for this review.

pool.question: A consumer says, "My coverage is from my retirement with the school district." What is it?
choices: Medicaid: continue
Insurance through retirement: DQ
Part B coverage: continue
Not a coverage type; ignore it
pool.explanation: Retirement insurance is a DQ.

pool.question: A consumer has Medicare Parts A and B plus Medicaid, no work or VA insurance, and agrees to a few minutes. What is their status?
choices: Needs a callback
Not Interested
Qualified for transfer
DQ because of Medicaid
pool.explanation: Dual eligible consumers qualify if they pass everything else.

pool.question: A consumer says, "I'm on the VA health plan." What is it?
choices: Military coverage: DQ
Medicaid: continue
Not a DQ if they have Medicare too
Medicare Part A: continue
pool.explanation: VA coverage is a DQ.

pool.question: Which is TRUE about Medicare and the government?
choices: America's Health is a government agency
The specialist is a government employee
You work for Medicare
Medicare is a government program, but you are not from Medicare or the government
pool.explanation: Never claim government affiliation.

pool.question: A consumer's card is from their plan company instead of the red, white and blue card. Are they automatically DQ?
choices: Yes, always DQ
No; transfer immediately
Yes, code Not Interested
No; ask if they have their Medicare number
pool.explanation: Different card branch: "Okay, no problem, but you DO have your Medicare number, correct?"

pool.question: Which is a correct way to describe what the consumer may get from the review?
choices: They may find benefits their plan options could include
They will definitely get more money
Their premium will drop to zero
They are guaranteed a food card
pool.explanation: Keep it conservative with may.

pool.question: Consumers on Medicare are often missing out because...
choices: Everyone is on the wrong plan
Medicare cancels benefits every month
Plans change and many people never review their options
The government hides benefits on purpose
pool.explanation: Many people stay on the same plan without checking what may be available.

pool.question: A consumer says, "I've got Medicare but my husband's job insurance covers me first." What is it?
choices: Wrong Number
Medicare Part B: continue
Medicaid: continue
Insurance through work: DQ
pool.explanation: Employer coverage through a spouse's job is insurance through work.

pool.question: What do extra benefits depend on?
choices: Nothing; they're the same for all
The fronter's script
The plan, the area, and the person's eligibility
Only the consumer's age
pool.explanation: Benefits vary by plan, area and eligibility.

pool.question: A consumer says, "I don't know my parts, but I have the red, white and blue card." What does that tell you?
choices: They have Tricare; DQ
Nothing useful; code NI
They have Medicaid; DQ
They have Medicare; confirm Parts A and B and continue
pool.explanation: The card is the Medicare card. Confirm A and B and skip to Medicaid.

pool.question: Which consumers may qualify for a transfer?
choices: Anyone over 50
People with Medicare Parts A and B and no employer, retirement, military or tribal coverage
Only people with Medicaid
Anyone with any health insurance card
pool.explanation: Parts A and B, no DQ coverage.

pool.question: Where do extra benefits like a food card or flex card come from?
choices: Medicare sends them to everyone with Parts A and B
Certain plans that a licensed specialist reviews, not Medicare itself
Social Security
The fronter's company pays for them
pool.explanation: Extra benefits like food or flex cards may come through certain plans a licensed specialist reviews. Medicare itself doesn't send them.

pool.question: A consumer says, "No, I just got Medicaid." What does that mean for qualifying?
choices: They qualify, Medicaid is the same as Medicare
They have no Medicare Parts A and B, so it's a DQ
Ask for their Medicaid number and transfer
Code it as No Agent
pool.explanation: Medicaid only means no Medicare Parts A and B. That's a DQ.

pool.question: A consumer says, "I got Medicare and Medicaid." What does that mean?
choices: They're a DQ because of Medicaid
They may still qualify. Medicaid yes or no, you keep going
They need to cancel Medicaid first
Transfer without asking about work or VA
pool.explanation: With Parts A and B, Medicaid yes or no is fine. Keep going with the questions.

pool.question: Which of these is a DQ?
choices: Medicaid along with Medicare
A retiree health plan through a former employer
A Medicare plan the consumer chose themselves
No red, white and blue card, but they have Medicare
pool.explanation: Insurance through work or retirement is a DQ, including retiree Medicare Advantage plans.

pool.question: Which answer is NOT a DQ?
choices: "I have Tricare for Life."
"I'm covered by my husband's job."
"I have Medicaid through the state."
"I only have Part A."
pool.explanation: Medicaid is not a DQ. Military coverage, employer coverage and no Part B are.

pool.question: A consumer says, "So Medicare is giving me more money?" What's the compliant answer?
choices: "Yes, Medicare is doing an increase."
"That would be a great question for the agent once I get you there."
"Yes, you qualify for all of it."
"It's a state program."
pool.explanation: Never say the benefit comes from Medicare, never say yes to more money, and never imply a state program.

pool.question: When you're not sure if the consumer's coverage is a DQ, what do you do?
choices: Transfer and let the specialist sort it out
Code DQ to be safe
Ask one clarifying question: "Is that through a job or retirement?"
Skip the work or VA question
pool.explanation: One short clarifying question, then read the DQ line or keep going.

pool.question: A consumer is 72. Do they qualify for Medicare by age?
choices: Only if they have low income
Yes, ALL people 65 and older qualify for Medicare
Only if they are a veteran
Only if they still work
pool.explanation: ALL people 65 and older qualify for Medicare, plus people under 65 with certain disabilities.

pool.question: A consumer is 58 and says they have Medicare because of a disability. Is that possible?
choices: No, Medicare is only for people 65 and older
No, they must mean Medicaid
Yes, people under 65 with certain disabilities can have Medicare
Only if they are a veteran
pool.explanation: Medicare covers ALL people 65 and older, plus people under 65 with certain disabilities.

pool.question: What do you need from the consumer to qualify them?
choices: Their full medical history
Their doctor's name and phone number
Their bank information
Name, state, ZIP and insurance status, and (if no card) whether they KNOW their Medicare or Social Security number
pool.explanation: You never ask them to read or give a Medicare or Social Security number. You only ask whether they know one; the licensed agent handles the actual number.

pool.question: What is the Medicare card called in the script?
choices: The green card
The red, white and blue card
The flex card
The Medicaid card
pool.explanation: The Medicare card is the red, white and blue card.

pool.question: What is the first line of the script?
choices: Good afternoon, is now a good time?
Hey, good morning/afternoon (Customer Name)?
Hello, may I speak with the account holder?
Hi, this is Medicare calling for (Customer Name).
pool.explanation: The script opens with "Hey, good morning/afternoon (Customer Name)?"

pool.question: What comes right after "Hey, good morning/afternoon (Customer Name)?"
choices: The Medicaid question
The transfer ask
The intro with America's Health on a recorded line and the Parts A and B question
The work or VA question
pool.explanation: Next is the intro and first qualifying question.

pool.question: Complete the line: "That card, it IS exclusively for members who have..."
choices: Medicare Parts A and B.
a VA plan.
a food card already.
Medicaid.
pool.explanation: "That card, it IS exclusively for members who have Medicare Parts A and B."

pool.question: Which is the correct double-confirm line?
choices: Okay, and you have your Medicare card with you right now, correct?
Okay, perfect, and JUST to double confirm, that IS the red, white and blue card, correct?
Okay, perfect, and JUST to double confirm, you still have your Medicare plan, correct?
Okay, perfect and JUST to confirm you have Medicaid, correct?
pool.explanation: Read the double-confirm verbatim.

pool.question: What comes right after the double-confirm card question?
choices: The Medicaid question
The state and ZIP line
The work or VA question
The transfer ask
pool.explanation: Order: Parts A and B, card, Medicaid, state/ZIP, work or VA.

pool.question: Which is the correct Medicaid question?
choices: Perfect and do you receive Social Security along with your Medicare plan?
Perfect and how much Medicaid do you receive?
Perfect, and do you receive Medicaid along with your Medicare plan?
Are you on Medicaid instead of Medicare?
pool.explanation: Verbatim: "Perfect, and do you receive Medicaid along with your Medicare plan?"

pool.question: What comes right after the Medicaid question?
choices: Cold transfer
State and ZIP
Double-confirm the card
Work or VA
pool.explanation: After Medicaid, confirm state and ZIP.

pool.question: In the state and ZIP line, what are you told the consumer may be?
choices: GUARANTEED a new food card
APPROVED for a Part B refund
ENTITLED to some additional food benefits
OWED money by Medicare
pool.explanation: "It DOES look like you may be ENTITLED to some additional food benefits since the food prices have gone up."

pool.question: Which line is the exact LAST question?
choices: Okay, LAST question here, do you have insurance through your work or the VA?
Okay, LAST question here, do you work?
Okay, LAST question here, do you have any other insurance at all?
Okay, LAST question here, are you a veteran?
pool.explanation: Verbatim: "Okay, LAST question here, do you have insurance through your work or the VA?"

pool.question: What comes right after the work or VA question (when they say No)?
choices: The transfer ask: "Perfect, well that is EVERYTHING I need..."
The double-confirm card question
The DNC disclaimer
The Medicaid question
pool.explanation: No to work or VA continues to the transfer ask.

Oh (Customer's Name), changing your insurance is ONLY something you can do. I don't even have the power to do that. There have just been some new allowances and new benefits that have JUST become available. We're just here to facilitate your free review.

Well, I understand, but you've worked your whole life for these Medicare benefits. Give the agent JUST a few minutes to review and compare your plan to make SURE you're not missing out on ANYTHING you may be entitled to.
That would be a great question for the agent once I get you there.

choices: I understand. Well, do you have the red, white and blue card by chance?
Perfect, and do you receive Medicaid along with your Medicare plan?
There must have been a mistake. Thank you for your time, have a great day.
Okay, LAST question here, do you have insurance through your work or the VA?
pool.explanation: Ask about the red, white and blue card.

pool.question: The consumer says "I have a Humana card, not that one." What do you say?
choices: Okay, no problem, but you DO have your Medicare number, correct?
There must have been a mistake. Thank you for your time, have a great day.
Perfect, and do you receive Medicaid along with your Medicare plan?

pool.question: At the double-confirm, the consumer says "I'm not giving my number out." What do you say?

Oh, there must have been a mistake. Thank you for your time, have a great day.
I understand, but MANY people are finding out RIGHT now that they ACTUALLY qualify for WAY more than they're receiving.

Don't transfer. Read an EXTRA NOT INTERESTED rebuttal, then go back to "Give them JUST a few minutes to go over them with you, okay?"
Read the DNC disclaimer
Transfer them anyway

Alright so you'll hear ringing, don't hang up, it's Medicare picking up okay?
Alright please hold, I'm going to introduce you to the specialist now okay?
Alright so the specialist will call you back in a few minutes okay?

You're definitely going to love this new plan.

pool.question: A consumer asks "Which plan is best for me?" Which rebuttal fits?
choices: That would be a great question for the agent once I get you there.

pool.question: A consumer says "I don't have time for this." Which rebuttal fits?
choices: Oh, so either you or a family member went online and expressed interest in a free review. We're just here to facilitate that for you.

Oh, let me assure you (customer's name), I'm not asking for any credit card or banking information. I'm with America's Health. We work with over 25 different health insurance providers. We're just here to facilitate your free review.
Oh, let me assure you this will be SUPER brief. I just have 3 SUPER quick questions and I'll bring the agent on.
I understand, but MANY people are finding out RIGHT now that they ACTUALLY qualify for WAY more than they're receiving.

pool.question: Complete the rebuttal: "The difference is WE work with over..."
choices: 5 government agencies
25 different health insurance providers
every insurance company in America
100 different Medicare offices

pool.question: A consumer grumbles, "You people are so annoying, what do you want?" What do you do?
choices: Read the DNC disclaimer and end the call
Code DQ
Stay calm, rebut and continue
Hang up without coding
pool.explanation: Rude is not DNC. Rebut and continue.

pool.question: A consumer says, "Take me off your list." What do you do?
choices: Transfer them so the specialist can handle it
Rebut once, then DNC if they repeat it
Code Not Interested
Read the DNC disclaimer verbatim, end the call, code DNC
pool.explanation: Never rebut past a DNC request.

choices: Okay, we'll try you again at a better time. Have a great day
Sorry about that, we'll put you on the Medicare do not call list, have a great day
No problem, I'll remove you, but first give the agent JUST a few minutes
No problem, I'll add you to our internal do not call list immediately and you won't receive any further calls from our company. We do apologize for any inconvenience, have a great day.

pool.question: Where is the ONLY place you ask for permission on the call?
choices: The Medicaid question
The ringing line
The opening greeting

"That would be a great question for the agent once I get you there."
"I'm calling from Medicare about your benefits."
"you may be ENTITLED to some additional food benefits"

choices: "In the meantime, how's that weather out there today?"
"do you receive Medicaid along with your Medicare plan?"
"We're just here to facilitate your free review"
"If you transfer, you're guaranteed a card worth money every month."

It makes the call longer
Nothing is guaranteed, so you can't promise what they'll qualify for
It's a sales trick

Stay on the full call
Introduce the consumer and their benefits
Read the DNC disclaimer

Transfer
Hung-Up Transfer
Conference Ended

DNC
Wrong Number
DQ

Code DNC

Code Dead Air

No Agent
Transfer
Hung-Up Transfer

Skip them
Ask only the ZIP code
Ask only the Medicaid question

Skip the ZIP line
Rebut each objection and go right back each time

Fluff, work or VA question, ringing line, transfer ask
Transfer ask, work or VA question, fluff, ringing line
Work or VA question, transfer ask, ringing line, fluff, stay silent when the agent picks up

Oh, let me assure you this will be SUPER brief. I just have 3 SUPER quick questions and I'll bring the agent on.
